record.tranche_reason: Reports before/after outcomes for a rank-1 weight projection that removes a refusal direction, testing its practical effect on refusal and capability measures.
record.gate_note: The article reports vendor-provided model-card outcomes for one edited model. The 13-model geometry summary and the original paper's claims are cited background, not results from this study. Direction-estimation details are described as method, not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The post reports before/after refusal and capability numbers for one released model edited by difference-in-means weight orthogonalization (Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-FP8). That is the original recipe applied in a new model setting, bearing on V2 and on the ablation and capability parts of V1. All numbers are vendor model-card values, not independently reproduced.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a single residual-stream direction mediates refusal and that a rank-1 weight projection removes it, cutting refusal from 64–99% to 0–6% with capabilities within ±1.3 points on one Qwen3.8-27B build. They caveat that removal leaves disclaimers, that refusal is 'redundantly encoded', and that capability cost depends on layer and strength; these caveats are asserted without measurements.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction, described for the production build as a massive-activation-masked estimate, then orthogonalizes residual-writing weights. This is a permanent weight edit rather than an activation-only ablation; the article does not report the original paper's addition intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The direction is estimated at layer 38, selected as the layer where it is most concentrated; the article says using the wrong layer or projecting more aggressively can reduce reasoning performance, but gives no comparative measurements for those choices.
record.problems: The before/after results are vendor-reported model-card values and explicitly not independently reproduced. Only one edited model is evaluated; no uncertainty estimates or null-direction controls are reported. The article does not provide individual benchmark results for thinking-enabled evaluation, and capability comparisons cover a limited set of benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported outcomes relevant to the claim were left out.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal. Any separate activation-ablation experiment. Null or random-direction controls.
Other released models, and independent reproduction.
Not tested. The redundancy statement is an assertion with no measurement of affine, cone or multi-direction structure.
Thinking-on before-edit refusal rates, so the effect in reasoning mode is not shown. No dedicated reasoning models.

record.verdict_notes: This is a vendor blog promoting its own abliterated model, and all numbers are model-card values the post says were not independently reproduced. There are no uncertainty estimates or controls, and only one model. The reader's V4 'supports' label is dropped: residual refusal and disclaimers are not evidence of a multi-direction structure, and the redundancy claim has no data. The reader's V8 label is dropped because there is no thinking-on baseline. Under V1, failing to test addition is untested, not limits_scope. The 13-model description is cited background from the original paper, not a result of this post.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests, nor report a separate activation-ablation experiment.
Does not report outcomes across multiple released models or independent reproduction.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
Does not identify or compare an affine set, cone, or multiple individual refusal directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages.
Tests a thinking-enabled setting on this model, not a range of dedicated reasoning models or reasoning-training methods.

tranche.reason: It applies the original difference-in-means plus weight-orthogonalization recipe, with a massive-activation-masked variant, to a new model (Qwen3.8-27B hybrid-attention, FP8) and reports before/after refusal and capability numbers. That is a new setting with a result on the claim. T2 (the reader's call) doesn't fit because the method is not different.

source_check.notes: The pack had no [lN] ids on its verdicts, so l1–l3 were assigned in pack order. OrcaRouter publishes the checkpoint itself (huggingface.co/orcarouter/...) and sells access, so 'vendor-reported' means self-reported, with no judge, controls or uncertainty stated. The thinking-on result (≤1.7% everywhere) and WikiText-2 perplexity 6.96 are not in the checked rows. The redundancy and layer-dependence caveats are assertions without numbers, so they support no verdict.
